label: Iris Blades
blurb: A real camera aperture shuts and opens again over the cut: a ring of straight blades swings in from the rim, each one turning as it closes, so the opening is a rounded polygon that shrinks to nothing and then irises back out on the incoming shot. The blade edges catch a thin line of light and the picture beyond them falls off into the body of the lens. Set the number of blades, how far they twist as they close, and whether the iris shuts and opens or only opens on the new shot.
